- Overestimate prices when sentiment is negative (especially strong negative sentiment), especially in early forecast periods.  
- Underestimate prices after strong upward spikes (e.g., >75) if sentiment turns mildly negative or neutral — model tends to overcorrect downward.  
- Forecast tends to lag in mean reversion — true prices often overshoot forecast by 1–2 days after a sharp move, then correct.  
- When sentiment is positive and prices are rising, model often overestimates the peak and then underestimates the subsequent decline.  
- In low-volatility periods, model overestimates mean price; in high-volatility periods, it underestimates extremes.  
- Forecast horizon 30d is prone to “early peak” bias — model peaks too soon, then drops too fast, missing sustained trend.  
- If sentiment is consistently negative over 3–5 days, model should reduce forecast slope and avoid sharp upward revisions.  
- When sentiment turns from negative to positive, model often fails to adjust forecast upward quickly — delay in “sentiment catch-up” bias.
